title: Coding Set 10: Bitwise Uniqueness & Regex Validation
description: Reported HCL coding problems: single non-duplicate element via XOR and Java-style regular expression validation.

problems.title: Element Occurring Once While All Others Appear Twice
problems.statement: Given an integer array A of odd size N where every element except one appears exactly twice, find and print the single unique element in O(N) time and O(1) extra space.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Odd integer N.
Line 2: N space-separated integers.

starterCode.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n = data[0]
ans = 0
for x in data[1:1+n]:
    ans ^= x
print(ans)

problems.timeComplexity: O(N) using XOR properties (`x ^ x = 0`, `x ^ 0 = x`).
edgeCases: Negative integers work seamlessly with two's complement XOR

problems.title: Java Regex-Based Identifier & Email Validator
problems.statement:
Given N input lines, each starting with a tag (`ID` or `EMAIL`) followed by a space and a token string (no internal spaces), validate each token:
- `ID`: valid Java identifier of length 1..30 starting with `[a-zA-Z_]` followed by `[a-zA-Z0-9_]*` (note: exclude `$` for this rule) and NOT in the reserved set `{class, public, static, void, int, if, else, return}`.
- `EMAIL`: local part `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+`, `@`, domain `[a-zA-Z0-9-]+`, `.` and 2-to-6-letter TLD `[a-zA-Z]{2,6}` (no consecutive dots in local part).
Print `VALID` or `INVALID` per line.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Integer N.
Next N lines: `<TYPE> <TOKEN>`.

testCases.input:
4
ID emp_01
ID class
EMAIL dev.hcl@hcltech.com
EMAIL bad..dot@hcl.com

testCases.note: Single domain label required before TLD here

testCases.input:
3
EMAIL a@b.in
EMAIL a@b.c
EMAIL test-1@org.tech

starterCode.python:
import sys, re

lines = sys.stdin.read().splitlines()
n = int(lines[0].strip())
# Write your solution here

solutions.python:
import sys, re

lines = [ln.strip() for ln in sys.stdin.read().splitlines() if ln.strip()]
n = int(lines[0])
reserved = {'class', 'public', 'static', 'void', 'int', 'if', 'else', 'return'}
id_re = re.compile(r'^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]{0,29}$')
email_re = re.compile(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9_-]|\.(?=[a-zA-Z0-9_-]))*@[a-zA-Z0-9-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,6}$')
out = []
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    kind, tok = lines[i].split()
    if kind == 'ID':
        ok = bool(id_re.match(tok)) and tok not in reserved
    else:
        ok = bool(email_re.match(tok))
    out.append('VALID' if ok else 'INVALID')
print('\n'.join(out))

problems.timeComplexity: O(L) per token where L <= 100 (anchored non-backtracking regex).
edgeCases: Leading or trailing dots in email local part ('.lead@...' or 'lead.@...') must be rejected
Consecutive dots ('bad..dot@...') rejected via positive lookahead
Java keywords (`class`, `return`) rejected even though they match `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`
